learning: If slalom max_error falls to 0.06 m or below with line losses at or below 2 per run, look-ahead was the remaining slalom limit and the next lever is controller tuning. If oval or s-bend completion drops below the iteration-4 levels (20 of 20 and 18 of 20), revert to y = 0.06 m. If the slalom loses the line more than 2 times per run with progress below 0.2, widen the spread to x = ±0.032 m.
notes: Geometry is the Builder's y = 0.07 m proposal with every other field unchanged. The controller is the iteration-4 controller, held constant so the look-ahead change is the only variable. Full measurement set requested.
rationale: Iteration 4 (0.6 kg, sensors at y = 0.06 m, controller kp 2.4, ki 0.2, kd 0.6, base_speed 1.3) is the best race so far at 649.6. The oval completes 20 of 20 with max_error 0.0139 m. The s-bend completes 18 of 20. The slalom still fails 0 of 20, but progress rose to 0.278 and max_error is 0.0638 m, just above the 0.06 m limit, with 1.05 line losses per run. The Builder's proposal moves all five sensors to y = 0.07 m and keeps the spread at x = ±0.024 m, body, wheels, track, sensor size and mass unchanged. This is the step the Integrator's rule calls for: slalom max_error at or above 0.06 m with line losses at or below 2 per run. Both conditions hold, and the widen-spread trigger (line losses above 2 with progress below 0.2) does not fire. The controller is kept exactly as in iteration 4. The Builder's intent is to isolate look-ahead, and changing the controller in the same race would confound that. I expect slalom max_error to move toward 0.06 m or below. The risk is extra oscillation on the oval and s-bend, which I will judge from the race data. The package is therefore the iteration-4 controller on the Builder's y = 0.07 m geometry.
